newsitem.title: USA: Bells, GTE, FCC chief criticize phone proposal.
newsitem.headline: Bells, GTE, FCC chief criticize phone proposal.

text.p: A trio of local phone companies and Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt Friday criticized the proposal offered by AT&T Corp, Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp to reform access charges and universal service.

Echoing the comments of consumer advocates who charge that the plan will raise local phone rates, Hundt said: "I don't think that Congress intended to have us raise residential basic dialtone like AT&T and Bell Atlantic proposed -- and I think I am reading Congress right on this."
Meanwhile, BellSouth Corp, U S West and GTE Corp called the plan "astounding" and "suspect."

The three carriers said they "are united in their reaction to this astounding proposal which will undermine more than six successful years of price cap regulation and threaten universal service in rural areas across America."
The carriers urged the FCC to give "this biased plan the short shrift it deserves."

AT&T, Bell Atlantic, and NYNEX proposed a plan they said would cut the charges long-distance carriers pay to access the local phone network by $2.5 billion a year and cut consumer phone bills by more than $400 million a year.
